# Environment variables

<p class="cli-lead">Variables the CLI reads, for CI, containers and scripts.</p>

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `CLAVIS_TOKEN` | Machine or agent token. Used instead of `clavis login`, for CI. |
| `CLAVIS_SERVER` | Server URL, like `--server`. |
| `CLAVIS_ORG`, `CLAVIS_PROJECT`, `CLAVIS_ENV` | Like `--org`, `--project`, `--env`. Override `.clavis.yaml`. |
| `CLAVIS_AGENT` | Agent identity for `clavis mcp`, like `--agent`. |
| `CLAVIS_CREDENTIAL_FILE` | Keep the login token in this file (mode `0600`) instead of the OS keychain. Useful in containers. |
| `CLAVIS_CACHE_DIR` | Where the offline cache lives. |
| `CLAVIS_SERVER_FINGERPRINT` | Expected SHA-256 of a self-signed server's certificate or public key. Trusts it without a prompt. |
| `CLAVIS_CA_CERT` | PEM file(s) with your own certificate authority, added to the system roots. Separate several with `:`. |
| `CLAVIS_TRUST_FILE` | Where trusted self-signed servers are stored. Default: `trusted-servers.json` in the config folder. |
| `NO_COLOR` | Turn off colors. They are also off when output isn't a terminal. |

Server settings (`CLAVIS_TLS`, `CLAVIS_SERVER_BASE_URL`,
`CLAVIS_SETUP_TOKEN`, ...) are described in the self-hosting guide.

## Examples

<p class="cli-example-title">CI with a machine token</p>

```sh
export CLAVIS_TOKEN=clv_mt_…
clavis run --project web-app --env production ./deploy.sh
```
